styles.label: Culture
styles.blurb: Gold Museum, colonial La Candelaria and the salt cathedral.

styles.label: Food
styles.blurb: Ajiaco, arepas and market food tours.

styles.label: Art
styles.blurb: Botero, murals and the Museo de Arte Miguel Urrutia.

stays.why: Walk to the Gold Museum, Plaza de Bolívar and Botero Museum. Lively by day, quiet and a bit rough-edged at night.
Best for restaurants, bars and nightlife; safe to walk in the evening. Far from the historic sights.
Central, good cafés and cheaper than Zona Rosa. A short ride to both the old town and the north.
Calm, leafy and close to the airport side of town. Sunday flea market and good food. Farthest from La Candelaria.

food: Try ajiaco (potato and chicken soup), bandeja paisa and arepas. Lunch menus (almuerzo) cost about COP$15,000–30,000.
Fruit is the highlight: try lulo, feijoa, granadilla and maracuyá at a market like Paloquemao or La Perseverancia.
Book a food tour in La Candelaria or Chapinero to taste safely and learn the names.
Coffee: order tinto for a small black coffee. Specialty cafés in Chapinero and Zona Rosa serve single-origin beans.
Street food is cheap but pick busy stalls. Drink bottled or filtered water; tap water is not for everyone.
more_time: Ride the TransMiCable to Ciudad Bolívar for views and murals — go with a local guide.
Day trip to Zipaquirá salt cathedral, about 1.5 hours by road; the Turistren steam train runs several times a week.
Hike or take the cable car up Monserrate on a clear morning; check the day's weather first.

recommend.why: Three nights covers the Gold Museum, La Candelaria, Monserrate and a food tour without rushing, and leaves room for one rainy afternoon.

month_notes: January: dry-ish, about 13 rain days. Cool nights near 8°C — pack a jacket.
February: similar to January, about 16 rain days. Mornings are usually clearest.
March: the wettest month, about 24 rain days. Plan indoor sights and carry a rain jacket.
April: still wet, about 20 rain days. Short heavy afternoon showers are common.
May: about 19 rain days. Mild days around 19°C; layers help.
June: about 16 rain days. Cool and often overcast.
July: about 16 rain days and the coolest highs near 18°C. Bring a warm layer.
August: drier, about 10 rain days. A good month for walking and views.
September: the driest month, about 8 rain days. Best odds of clear skies for Monserrate.
October: wetter again, about 16 rain days. Keep a backup indoor plan.
November: about 22 rain days. One of the wettest months.
December: about 14 rain days. Festive lights and busy streets; book ahead.

climate_guide.summary: High-altitude tropical city: mild all year, cool nights, and rain possible in any month. September is driest, March and November wettest.

items.title: Mild days, cool nights
items.text: Highs stay near 18–20°C all year; lows around 8–10°C. Bring a jacket for evenings.

items.title: Rain in every month
items.text: Expect 8–24 rain days per month. Showers are often short and heavy in the afternoon.

items.title: Driest: August and September
items.text: About 8–10 rain days. Best odds for Monserrate views and day trips.

items.title: Wettest: March and November
items.text: About 22–24 rain days. Plan museums and cafés, and carry an umbrella.

items.title: Altitude about 2,600 m
items.text: Take the first day easy. Drink water and skip heavy exercise until you adjust.

items.title: What to pack
items.text: Layers, a waterproof jacket, comfortable shoes for hills and cobblestones, and sunscreen for sunny spells.

transit.best: TransMilenio for cheap main routes; taxi or app for evenings and hills.

modes.text: No metro yet. Don't plan around rail inside the city.
TransMilenio BRT and green SITP buses use a rechargeable Tullave card. Fares about COP$3,600 (TransMilenio) and COP$3,200 (SITP); the card costs about COP$8,000. Crowded at rush hour.

Uber, Cabify, DiDi and InDrive work but are officially unregulated; drivers may ask you to sit in front. Call taxis by dispatch or app, never hail on the street; check the meter starts and lock doors.
TransMiCable gondola links Ciudad Bolívar to TransMilenio; a separate tourist cable car climbs Monserrate.
No intercity trains; Turistren steam trains run to Zipaquirá several times a week.
Not recommended: heavy traffic, restricted plates and confusing parking. Use buses, taxis and apps instead.
Good in La Candelaria, Chapinero and Zona Rosa by day. Hills and uneven pavements; avoid unlit streets at night.
